title: Arancini
subtitle: Sicilian fried rice balls stuffed with ragù and mozzarella
excerpt: Sicily's great street food: balls of saffron risotto rice packed around a core of slow-cooked meat ragù and mozzarella, coated in breadcrumbs, and fried until the outside is deep gold and shatteringly crisp and the cheese inside has melted.

recipe.sourceNotes: Arancini (little oranges) are the defining street food of Sicily, sold from rosticcerie (rotisseries) throughout the island, particularly in Palermo and Catania. The name comes from their golden colour and rounded shape. There are two main camps: the rounded shape (arancina) typical of the western half of the island, and the pointed conical shape (arancino) of the east, particularly Catania. The filling also varies by region: ragù and mozzarella is the most common, but a version with burro (butter, béchamel, and ham) is traditional in eastern Sicily. The rice is flavoured with saffron, giving it a golden hue before frying. Arancini are typically made from leftover risotto, making them a thrifty, practical dish, but they are elaborate enough to be considered festive and appear at celebrations.

content.text: The rice must be cold and firm before you shape the arancini. If it is warm or loose, they will fall apart in the oil. Make the rice a day ahead if possible. Refrigerate the shaped balls for 30 minutes before frying to help them hold together. Fry in small batches at 180°C; do not crowd the pan or the temperature will drop.

items.preparation: cut into 1 cm cubes; for stuffing

content.text: Make the risotto: fry the onion briefly, add the rice, stir in hot stock ladle by ladle until absorbed (about 18 minutes total), adding the saffron water partway through. Remove from heat, stir in butter and parmesan, season. Spread onto a tray to cool, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.

Make the ragù filling: brown the mince, add the tinned tomatoes, season, and cook down until thick and almost dry, about 20 minutes. Leave to cool. With wet hands, take a large tablespoon of cold rice, flatten in your palm, place a cube of mozzarella and a teaspoon of ragù in the centre, and close the rice around it to form a ball. Press firmly. Repeat.

Set up three shallow bowls: flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs. Roll each ball in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs. Refrigerate for 30 minutes. Heat oil to 180°C and fry in batches of 3 or 4 for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden all over. Drain on kitchen paper and serve hot.
